A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WhiSPA study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendix A.1–A.4. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original psychological prediction experiments, human-annotated valence evaluation, ablations, and linguistic analyses in Tables 2–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations in Table 5 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Pooling, semantic/PsychEmb alignment, replacement/projection variants, and cosine/NCE objectives remain unchanged. WhiSPA-1034 applies the existing procedure with larger models; no new algorithmic component is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions use WTC and HiTOP, ten self-supervised psychological dimensions, eleven downstream psychological outcomes, and the 300 annotated audio segments. The larger-model experiments retain this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 5 adds evaluated SBERT-1024 and Whisper-1024 variants and extends SBERT-384 comparisons to all eleven downstream scales beyond the selected scales in v2 Table 5. Existing baseline families remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds a configuration pairing whisper-medium with all-roberta-large-v1, both producing 1024-dimensional embeddings, alongside the original 384-dimensional configuration. Person-level averaging, ten-fold ridge regression, Pearson correlation/MSE metrics, and the stated data split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new scaling study tests whether alignment remains effective with larger student and teacher models. Existing loss/component ablations, embedding-overlap analysis, SBERT-concatenation test, and n-gram analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Paired t-tests, p < .05 significance reporting, and Benjamini–Hochberg correction for n-gram correlations remain unchanged. The added table follows existing reporting practices; no new run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals are introduced.

E6.justification: v3 Table 5 adds larger-model outcomes: INT/PCL correlations are .67/.41 for WhiSPA-1034, .57/.28 for Whisper-1024, and .65/.37 for SBERT-1024. Figure 4 replaces the small-model plot and also revises self-supervised W2V2B/HuBERT values without clarifying aggregation, preventing direct interpretation as same-setting gains. Existing result-table values are retained.

T1.justification: The cosine and NCE loss definitions in Equations 1–2 and their mathematical explanations are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic/psychological alignment, improved speech representations, and limited benefit from an additional text encoder. The scaling experiment supplies further supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the scaling results as evidence of generalizability and attributes more consistent teacher outperformance to enhanced context retention in larger models. The teacher-capacity and acoustic-information limitations remain, with Appendix A.4 updated to reference SBERT-1024.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the added model checkpoints and approximate parameter counts, adds a 525-participant HiTOP description alongside Table 1’s unchanged 524 post-filtering participants, and identifies WTC’s Stony Brook Health Program provenance. Existing training details and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning remain unchanged. Added introductory citations already appeared elsewhere in v2, while the Sartori–Orrù reference receives missing year and venue metadata.

P1.justification: v3 repairs the corrupted introductory sentence and spacing, adds a scaling-results paragraph, and makes localized appendix and cross-reference edits. Overall section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5 and redraws and moves v2’s appendix Figure 8 into the main text as Figure 4, updating its model legend and caption. Existing tables and appendix figures are relocated or renumbered; the other figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The larger-model comparisons address v2’s limited validation across model capacities, while the repaired introduction improves readability. These are useful but limited gains. Both student and teacher change together, so the context-retention explanation is not isolated, and the new claim of teacher outperformance on 7 of 11 outcomes conflicts with the 8 shown by Table 5’s displayed correlations.
